newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed a touch lower on Thursday and dealers said the market was awaiting 'any good news' to boost business.
"Prices are likely to consolidate at the current level in the near-term," said one dealer. But, he saw scope for further moderate rises as soon as economic data support the market.
Guilder-bonds were hurt by profit taking, in a market that was mostly futures driven.
"Cash trade was mainly in the July 1998 and January 2006 bonds," said one dealer. "Buyers will return if the December bund futures contract stays well above the 100-level," said one.
The December bund futures contracts were trading at 100.26 at 1650 GMT, after hitting a low of 100.10 during the session.
The market ignored the Bundesbank decision to leave interest rates unchanged as the outcome was broadly expected and German and U.S. unemployment data were also brushed aside.
The spread with Germany widened a little during today's session, but dealers said the gap was too small to trigger switching.
The spread between the January 2006 bond and the German April 2006 widened to minus 14 today, but returned to yesterday's level of minus 12.
"If the gap widens to minus 15, investors could start selling their Dutch bonds and step into bunds," said one dealer.
Dealers said the outcome of the U.S. Treasury auction could also spark a new uptrend starting in the U.S.
The July 1998 bond slipped 0.04 to 104.23/31, bid yield 3.59 percent.
The January 2006 bond closed off 0.20 at 101.34/42.
The long Dutch 2023 bond was down 0.46 at 111.36/56, with a bid yield of 6.58 percent or 19 basis points below the 2024 bund versus minus 21 on Wednesday.
